narrow: The every-design upper bound is false even after design-conditional centering. In the scalar \(\lambda=1\) model, put only order \(T/\sqrt N\) exact design points near \(z_0\) and the remainder near a remote point. Then \(g_{1T}(z_0)=O(N^{-1/2})\) and \(R_D=O(N^{-1})\), but a donor-fold mean lies several \(N^{-1/2}\) units to one side with probability bounded away from zero. The first-coercive rule then skips the local cluster and fits the remote cluster, producing constant conditional squared error. The retained treated-mean lower bound is a genuine consequence of the original claim and is proved here.
This replacement removes all dependencies on the deleted obstruction and on the invalid Wald upper construction, retaining only the proved honest-length converse.

narrow: The specific Wald interval is not uniformly honest under boundedness alone. If treated increments are Bernoulli with probability \(\gamma/n\), then with probability tending to \(e^{-\gamma}\) all treated observations are zero and their sample variance is zero. Taking \(T\) and \(N\) sufficiently large makes every added bias radius \(o(n^{-1})\), so the interval misses the target \(\gamma/n\). The lower expected-length half remains valid at the corrected rate and is proved here.
This replacement removes the deleted obstruction dependency and wires the corrected lower-bound proof to its two explicit testing families.
